messages:
amy-support: Hey team, customer (AcmeHealth) just opened a high-sev ticket: p99 latency on hosted API jumped ~3x over the last 48h and some requests are returning 504s. Sample req ids: rwd-req-8a1f, rwd-req-8a3b. Model: rwd-13b-q4 (hosted pool: prod-eu-a100-80gb). They reported heavier context lengths recently (~>3k tokens).

jordan-sre: @amy-support can you paste a few logs / attach a flame or trace? Any CPU/GPU OOMs in node logs?

amy-support: attaching excerpt from the customer-provided trace and our serving logs: 
```
2026-03-16T10:12:04Z INFO serve: start request rwd-req-8a1f model=rwd-13b-q4 seq_len=3200 batch=12
2026-03-16T10:12:04Z WARN allocator: kv_cache_size=11.8GB -> 19.6GB (growth +7.8GB)
2026-03-16T10:12:05Z ERROR infer: p99 response time 3.4s (baseline 1.1s)
2026-03-16T10:12:06Z ERROR gpu0: failed to allocate 268435456 bytes
2026-03-16T10:12:06Z ERROR infer: request rwd-req-8a1f failed: downstream timeout
```

Customer repro steps they gave: send 8 parallel requests with ~3.2k token prompts (long convo history + 512 tokens target) and batch_size=12 on our hosted endpoint.

kevin-runtime: Thanks. That allocator log + growth spike looks like KV cache growth combined with large batch parallelism. Two quick checks: 1) are we honoring per-request max_kv_cache or leaking across requests? 2) what's the per-shard GPU free memory at the time?

maria-ml: I'm seeing similar in eval infra last week when multi-user sessions had unbounded prefix caching. Could be prefix caching never evicted due to key mismatch. We recently rolled a change to enable sticky KV across short-lived sessions — might be the culprit.

jordan-sre: I pulled node metrics for prod-eu-a100-80gb between 10:00-10:30 UTC: GPU mem used baseline 24GB -> spikes to 48-52GB on affected hosts, p95 load doubled. No kernel OOMs but allocator failures surfaced in logs.

amy-support: Customer is blocking, asking for immediate mitigation. Any temporary knobs we can flip on hosted pool?

kevin-runtime: Immediate mitigations we can try (ordered by risk):
- Reduce per-request concurrency for that customer (throttle parallel requests to 2) :low-risk
- Enforce per-request max_kv_tokens (cap history length) for their API key :low-risk
- Reduce default batch_size on prod-eu pool from 12 -> 4 :medium-risk (affects throughput)
- Restart a subset of runtime replicas to reclaim fragmented GPU memory :medium-risk
- Rollback recent sticky-KV change to 1.2.3 -> 1.2.2 on a canary subset :higher-risk

maria-ml: I can push a quick feature-flag to disable sticky KV for the prod-eu pool for the customer’s sub-tenant. That will avoid cross-request retention of KV.

jordan-sre: I'll schedule a rolling restart of 3 shards (non-overlapping) in prod-eu to reclaim slabs. We'll coordinate with deploy-bot. 

alex-deploy-bot: @jordan-sre scheduled rolling-restart runtime/pool/prod-eu at 2026-03-16T11:05:00Z (3 pods). Will perform pre-checks and report status.

sam-customer-success: I've told the customer we're applying throttles and will monitor; asked for permission to truncate conversation length on their side as well. They're ok with temporary caps. :thumbsup:

amy-support: Action list for now: 1) throttle their key to 2 concurrent requests, 2) apply per-key max_kv_tokens=2048, 3) canary disable sticky-KV for prod-eu for that customer, 4) rolling restart 3 shards.

kevin-runtime: Adding repro steps we used to reproduce locally (minimal):
1) Configure local serving to use rwd-13b-q4 on a dev A100 vm.
2) Set batch_size=12, parallel_clients=8.
3) Send prompt with ~3200 tokens history + 512 generate (total ~3712 tokens).
4) Repeat until allocator log shows kv_cache growth > +6GB within a minute.

maria-ml: I also dumped allocator internals: 
```
[allocator] slab_pool: free_slots=120 used_slots=380 frag_ratio=0.63
[kv] total_entries=1_240_432 active_sessions=1_003 sticky_hits=86 sticky_evictions=1
```
Looks like many small sessions kept entries alive.

jordan-sre: After the rolling restart and throttles (11:05->11:20) we saw per-host GPU mem stable ~26GB, no new failed allocs logged. p99 for the customer's requests reduced to ~1.2s within 15m.

amy-support: Customer confirmed latency is back to normal in their next test. They saw a few transient 504s during the restart window but accepted.

kevin-runtime: Follow-ups:
- We'll implement a hard per-request KV cap (config flag) so a single request can't expand >3GB of KV.
- Add a periodic background KV compaction to evict entries not referenced in X minutes.
- Revert sticky-KV rollout until we have TTL-based eviction.
- Add a telemetry alert on kv_cache_growth rate (>= +5GB/min) to auto-throttle noisy clients.

maria-ml: I'll own the sticky-KV rollback and add TTL eviction (PR inbound, aiming EOD).

jordan-sre: I'll add a runbook step: on kv_growth spike, throttle keys >N parallel requests and perform rolling restart on a small subset. Also documenting how to safely drain shards.

amy-support: Thanks. I'll close the support ticket with the customer summary and the mitigation steps.

kevin-runtime: One more note for postmortem: investigate why batch_size=12 is still the default for this pool given average seq length. Might make sense to auto-select batch_size based on median seq length telemetry.

sam-customer-success: Customer asked for a post-incident summary and next steps — I'll coordinate a 1-pager once we have the rollback + TTL plan.

alex-deploy-bot: rolling-restart runtime/pool/prod-eu completed at 2026-03-16T11:18:30Z (3/3 pods restarted) :white_check_mark:

amy-support: Marking resolved from support side — will follow up if customer reopens. Thanks everyone. :tada:
